subject.title: Codex app-server emits notification:turn/started then goes silent; embedded run wedges for the full stuck-session recovery window

question: When a visible channel turn is aborted for missing progress, should OpenClaw retry/resume it automatically, emit a retryable failure and release the lane, or use a bounded hybrid policy by failure class?
rationale: The reports show that aborting alone can lose the accepted message or leave stale lane state; choosing delivery/retry semantics changes user-visible behavior and cannot be safely inferred from a timeout implementation.

options.title: Release and notify
options.body: Abort the stale run, atomically clear its ownership state, send one retryable failure through the originating channel, and let the next inbound message start cleanly.

options.title: Bounded automatic retry
options.body: Retry only classes with a demonstrably safe idempotency boundary, then fall back to a visible failure and lane release.

options.title: Resume-only recovery
options.body: Preserve and resume interrupted work where the runtime supports it, accepting greater implementation and state-consistency complexity.

recommendation.title: Release and notify
recommendation.body: Abort the stale run, atomically clear its ownership state, send one retryable failure through the originating channel, and let the next inbound message start cleanly.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked reliability-design and Codex liveness work make this the strongest available routing signal for the recovery-policy decision.
